abstract: Congenital teratoma of the oropharyngeal cavity is a unique clinical entity that poses immediate threats to the neonate in the postpartum period. Establishment of a secure airway is a primary goal after delivery; complete surgical resection is the subsequent guiding principle of management. Even more rare than teratomas confined to the oropharynx are tumors that extend into the intracranial cavity during development. Descriptions of these lesions in the medical literature are uncommon. In the majority of these reports, the tumors are associated with stillbirth, perinatal death, or significant morbidity after attempted resection. We present the rare case of a patient with congenital oropharyngeal teratoma with intracranial extension who has demonstrated long-term survival without any neurological or functional deficits. A unique delayed staged approach to resection of the extracranial and intracranial components of the tumor is described.
abstract_ja: 先天性口咽頭奇形腫は、出生後に新生児の気道確保を脅かす独特の臨床的病態である。口咽頭に限局する奇形腫よりさらに稀なのは、発生の過程で頭蓋内腔へ進展する腫瘍である。こうした病変の報告は医学文献上まれである。報告の多くは死産や周産期死亡、あるいは切除試行後の重大な障害と関連している。今回我々は、頭蓋外および頭蓋内の腫瘍成分に対して段階的に遅延切除を行った独自の治療法を記載し、神経学的および機能的欠損なく長期生存を得た口咽頭奇形腫（頭蓋内進展）の稀な症例を報告する。
